messages.content: I want to tighten up Oregon lodging now. Compare the full eight nights, but change the second coast stay to four nights and put the last night by PDX. So: Cannon Beach August 2-5, Newport or Yachats August 5-9, airport August 9-10. We need one room for Daniel, Owen, and me, and I do not want to discover that a quoted room only allows two people.

Understood. I’ll compare complete three-stop sequences for three guests: three nights on the northern coast, four on the central coast, and one near Portland airport. I’ll verify the actual sleeping setup and stated maximum occupancy, then include taxes, mandatory fees, parking, cancellation deadlines, and the drives between each stop. Nothing will be reserved.
Keep it to two sequences. I would rather have clear choices than a long hotel list.

Two combinations stand out on the current quotes. Sequence A is Inn at Cannon Beach, Hallmark Resort Newport, and Hampton Inn Portland Airport. Sequence B is Tolovana Inn, Adobe Resort in Yachats, and Hyatt Place Portland Airport/Cascade Station. Both can accommodate all three travelers in the specific room categories quoted; I’m checking the rate details before giving you the totals.
Start with A. What rooms are those, and what is the real total after tax and fees?

Sequence A uses an Inn at Cannon Beach deluxe room with two queen beds, maximum occupancy four, August 2-5. Three nights are $1,185, estimated lodging tax is $142.20, and the mandatory property fee is $30, for $1,357.20. Hallmark Resort Newport is an ocean-view room with two queen beds, maximum occupancy four, August 5-9. Four nights are $1,316, estimated tax is $158.92, and there is no separate resort fee, for $1,474.92. Hampton Inn Portland Airport is a two-queen room, maximum occupancy four, August 9-10, at $199 plus $31.84 estimated tax, totaling $230.84. The complete eight-night lodging total is $3,062.96.
And Owen is counted as a guest in all three quotes, not just assumed to share a bed?

Correct. Each search was priced for two adults and one 12-year-old. All three properties show three registered occupants on the quote, and each selected room has two queen beds with a stated capacity of four. There is no rollaway requirement or extra-person charge in those totals.
Give me cancellation and parking for A.

Inn at Cannon Beach is refundable through 6:00 p.m. Pacific on July 26; after that, the penalty is the first night plus tax. Self-parking is free, one vehicle per room. Hallmark Newport is refundable through 4:00 p.m. Pacific on July 29; a later cancellation costs one night plus tax. Its outdoor self-parking is free for one vehicle. Hampton PDX is refundable through 11:59 p.m. Pacific on August 8; after that, the first night plus tax is charged. Its lot is free during the hotel stay, but extended airport parking is not included. None of the three quotes requires a prepaid nonrefundable deposit.
Now B, same level of detail.

Sequence B starts at Tolovana Inn in a standard room with two queen beds, maximum occupancy four, August 2-5. The room is $1,041, estimated tax is $124.92, and the mandatory amenity fee is $36, totaling $1,201.92. Adobe Resort in Yachats is a non-view two-queen room, maximum occupancy four, August 5-9. Four nights are $1,164, estimated tax is $139.68, with no mandatory resort fee, totaling $1,303.68. Hyatt Place Portland Airport/Cascade Station is a two-queen room with a sofa sleeper, stated capacity five, August 9-10. It is $211 plus $33.76 estimated tax, totaling $244.76. The complete eight-night total is $2,750.36, which is $312.60 less than Sequence A.
What are the catches on B? The lower number is meaningful, but I do not want to trade away the trip to get it.

Tolovana is practical but less central: it is at the south end of Cannon Beach, roughly a 7-minute drive or about a 30-minute walk to the main downtown blocks. The quoted room is also a straightforward motel-style room rather than a cottage-style unit. Adobe is in Yachats, about 25 miles south of central Newport, so Newport attractions require roughly 35-40 minutes each way. The Hyatt Place is about a 7-minute drive from the PDX terminal and is surrounded by airport and retail development rather than a walkable neighborhood. The savings do not come from occupancy restrictions; they mainly reflect location and simpler room categories.
Cancellation and parking for B too.

Tolovana Inn is refundable through 3:00 p.m. Pacific on July 25, with a one-night-plus-tax penalty after that. Parking is free for one vehicle. Adobe Resort is refundable through 4:00 p.m. Pacific on July 28; after the deadline, the first night plus tax is charged. Parking is free in its surface lot. Hyatt Place is refundable through 11:59 p.m. Pacific on August 8, after which one night plus tax is due. Overnight self-parking is $10 plus $1.60 tax, and that amount is already included in the $244.76 total. No other mandatory parking or destination charge appears in Sequence B.
Lay out the driving. Include the airport-hotel move on the ninth, because that is why we changed the lodging split.

From PDX to either Cannon Beach hotel on August 2, allow about 1 hour 45 minutes without a long stop. On August 5, Inn at Cannon Beach to Hallmark Newport is about 2 hours 45 minutes direct; Tolovana to Adobe Yachats is about 3 hours 20 minutes direct. A sightseeing day on US-101 can easily make either transfer five to six hours. On August 9, Hallmark Newport to Hampton PDX is about 2 hours 40 minutes, while Adobe Yachats to Hyatt Place is about 3 hours 10 minutes. On August 10, Hampton is about 4 minutes from the rental-car return area and Hyatt Place about 7 minutes. The airport night removes the long coastal drive from departure morning in both sequences.
Which sequence would you actually narrow to? We care about using Newport as a base more than having a fancier airport hotel.

Sequence A is the more practical fit. Hallmark keeps the family in Newport for all four central-coast nights, avoids repeated 70-80 minute round trips from Yachats, and still gives a two-queen room verified for three guests. Inn at Cannon Beach is also easier for walking into town. Hampton is the simpler airport stop, but it does exactly what the final night needs. The $312.60 premium is mostly buying better positioning on seven coast nights, not airport amenities.
Can any sensible mix lower that without losing Newport? I am fine with Tolovana if the room and occupancy are solid.

Yes. Tolovana Inn plus Hallmark Newport plus Hampton PDX totals $2,907.68 for all eight nights. That is $155.28 below full Sequence A and keeps the four-night Newport base. Every room has two queen beds, allows four occupants, and is quoted for two adults and one 12-year-old. Parking is free at all three, and the applicable cancellation deadlines remain July 25 for Tolovana, July 29 for Hallmark, and August 8 for Hampton.

That mixed version sounds like the right working choice. Keep full A as the fallback, and retain B only as the lower-cost Yachats comparison. Add the transportation estimate so I can see the overall exposure, but do not book.

Saved without booking. Working lodging choice: Tolovana Inn August 2-5, Hallmark Resort Newport August 5-9, and Hampton Inn Portland Airport August 9-10, all in two-queen rooms confirmed for Marcus, Daniel, and Owen. Eight-night lodging is $2,907.68 including estimated taxes and mandatory fees, with free parking throughout. Cancellation deadlines are July 25 at 3:00 p.m., July 29 at 4:00 p.m., and August 8 at 11:59 p.m., all Pacific time. With the retained $2,065 round-trip flight, SUV, and fuel estimate, the working trip total is $4,972.68 before meals and activities. Full Sequence A remains the location-forward fallback at $3,062.96 lodging, or $5,127.96 with transportation. Sequence B remains the Yachats comparison at $2,750.36 lodging, or $4,815.36 overall. Nothing has been reserved.
